source.title: Regression in 2.46.0: $('Node').first() returns null for a node's error output in webhook executions (vm engine)

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

source.body:
### Bug Description

**Severity: high. The failure is silent and it affects the current stable release.**

In production webhook executions, an expression that reads items from a node set to "Continue (using error output)" resolves to `null` instead of the item. n8n shows no error, so downstream nodes silently receive `null`. In my case the whole parameter of a Redis node became null and the push failed with "Invalid argument type"; with other nodes it could silently write empty values (similar to the impact described in #41588).

It is a regression: it works up to 2.45.0 and fails from 2.46.0. Still failing on 2.47.5 and on the current stable 2.48.4. `N8N_EXPRESSION_ENGINE=legacy` is the only workaround I found, and the config marks `legacy` as soon to be deprecated.

Only the reference to the node that produced the error output fails. `$json` and a reference to the node right after the error output work. Inside a try/catch the expression throws `#<Object> could not be cloned.`

Related but different: #41588 / #42335 (1.x, Code node with task runners disabled, fixed in #42249). This is 2.x with the default `vm` engine. Forum thread: https://community.n8n.io/t/regression-in-2-46-0-node-first-returns-null-for-a-nodes-error-output-in-webhook-executions-fixed-by-n8n-expression-engine-legacy/329337

### To Reproduce

1. Import the workflow below (Webhook, a Code node "Thrower" that throws with "Continue (using error output)", a passthrough Code node on its error output, and a Set node "Check"), then publish it.
2. Call `GET /webhook/repro` on the production URL.
3. Compare the returned fields.

Result, 8-12 calls per version, identical every time:

| Version / engine | `$('Thrower').first().json.error` | `$('Thrower').first(1).json.error` | `$json.error` | try/catch around `$('Thrower').first(1)` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2.34.5, 2.40.0, 2.44.0, 2.45.0 | boom | boom | boom | OK |
| 2.46.0, 2.47.5, 2.48.4 (default engine) | **null** | **null** | boom | `ERR: #<Object> could not be cloned.` |
| 2.47.5, `N8N_EXPRESSION_ENGINE=legacy` | boom | boom | boom | OK |

Notes:
- Only webhook (production) executions fail. Running the same workflow with `n8n execute` on 2.47.5 passes.
- `N8N_EXPRESSION_ENGINE_ALLOW_WEBHOOK_ISOLATE_SKIP=false`, `N8N_EXPRESSION_ENGINE_LAZY_ACQUIRE=false` and `N8N_EXPRESSION_ENGINE_NATIVE_EVALUATION=false` do not change the result on 2.47.5.
- I only tested a Code node as the failing node.
- I did not find the commit. It is somewhere between n8n@2.45.0 and n8n@2.46.0.

<details><summary>Workflow JSON</summary>

```json
[{"id":"repro2","name":"repro webhook","active":false,"settings":{"executionOrder":"v1"},"nodes":[{"id":"n1","name":"Webhook","type":"n8n-nodes-base.webhook","typeVersion":2,"position":[0,0],"webhookId":"11111111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555","parameters":{"httpMethod":"GET","path":"repro","responseMode":"lastNode","responseData":"firstEntryJson","options":{}}},{"id":"n2","name":"Thrower","type":"n8n-nodes-base.code","typeVersion":2,"position":[220,0],"onError":"continueErrorOutput","parameters":{"jsCode":"throw new Error('boom');"}},{"id":"n3","name":"Pass","type":"n8n-nodes-base.code","typeVersion":2,"position":[440,100],"parameters":{"jsCode":"return $input.all();"}},{"id":"n4","name":"Check","type":"n8n-nodes-base.set","typeVersion":3.4,"position":[660,100],"parameters":{"mode":"manual","includeOtherFields":false,"assignments":{"assignments":[{"id":"a1","name":"first_default","type":"string","value":"={{ $('Thrower').first().json.error }}"},{"id":"a2","name":"first_1","type":"string","value":"={{ $('Thrower').first(1).json.error }}"},{"id":"a3","name":"json_error","type":"string","value":"={{ $json.error }}"},{"id":"a4","name":"pass_first","type":"string","value":"={{ $('Pass').first().json.error }}"},{"id":"a5","name":"try_catch","type":"string","value":"={{ (() => { try { $('Thrower').first(1); return 'OK' } catch (e) { return 'ERR: ' + e.message } })() }}"}]},"options":{}}}],"connections":{"Webhook":{"main":[[{"node":"Thrower","type":"main","index":0}]]},"Thrower":{"main":[[],[{"node":"Pass","type":"main","index":0}]]},"Pass":{"main":[[{"node":"Check","type":"main","index":0}]]}}}]
```

</details>

### Expected behavior

`$('Thrower').first().json.error` returns "boom", as on 2.45.0 and on the legacy engine.

### Debug Info

Reproduced with the official `docker.n8n.io/n8nio/n8n` images in throwaway containers (n8n CLI `import:workflow` + `publish:workflow`, then `n8n start`), default settings, no custom environment variables except those listed above. Not taken from the UI.

### Operating System

Docker Hardened Images / Alpine Linux v3.24 (official image), on an AlmaLinux 9 host

### n8n Version

2.47.5 (also 2.46.0 and 2.48.4)

### Node.js Version

26.13.0

### Database

SQLite (default)

### Execution mode

main (default)

### Hosting

self hosted

comments.author: grinem
comments.text: The `# could not be cloned` error points directly to V8 structured cloning failing when the `vm` engine serializes raw `runData` across the isolate boundary for error output branches (un-clonable `Error` prototype/property descriptors).
